deliverables.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE high-fidelity full-page product-detail website mockup image, tall portrait 1600 x 4000 desired. Clear readable desktop UI for CanveliqSoft. This is revision 2 after the customer said revision 1 was far too dense. The overriding goal is EFFORTLESS COMPREHENSION with premium styling.

VISUAL DESIGN: calm, spacious editorial software store. Light ivory-lavender #F7F6FC background, large white content areas, ink #101A33, navy #080F1E, purple #7952EB, cyan #00DCEB. Small dark glass nav at the top with CanveliqSoft logo, Collection, Work, About, Let's talk. Serif only for product name and one phrase. All section titles and body use highly readable modern sans serif. Main title 64px, section titles 36px, body 24px at 1600px width. 1.6 body line height. Generous 110px left/right page padding, comfortable 80–110px vertical gaps. A simple spacious centered single reading column. Max TWO columns within an individual section. No miniature text; no dense table grids; no walls of explanation. Use restrained fine rules between sections, minimal boxes. One navy hero preview and one navy final action band, everything else light. Very soft lavender accents only. Do not fill empty space with more content. Essential visible copy limited to about 280 words for the ENTIRE page outside the preview image. DO NOT add your own extra marketing paragraphs, headings, claims or captions. The supplied words are enough.

INFORMATION DESIGN: The same TEN blocks in order, but use progressive disclosure. The reader sees key facts first and opens details only when needed. An accordion has a crisp plus icon and a full-width 64px-height row; active row has a minus and only 2–3 short readable lines. A lightweight left reading-progress rail is ten small dots, ONLY the active label is shown, not a second table of contents. Every block has ONE normal-size title, not a tiny heading followed by a second giant marketing headline. Plenty of whitespace is intentional. The screenshot is full page and not forced to fit a single desktop viewport.
Order: 01 Product header; 02 Product preview; 03 Is this for you?; 04 What gets easier; 05 What's included; 06 A day with it; 07 How we deliver; 08 Investment; 09 Good to know; 10 Let's talk about your project. End with "You may also need" two simple horizontal text links, no extra card grids.

UX: Fit check appears as a simple "Check my fit · 3 quick questions" button, NOT all the questions on screen. Advanced features, exclusions, delivery details and trust terms use collapsed accordion rows. At bottom a narrow sticky bar with product name, heart Save and ONE large cyan "Discuss this solution →" button. At section10 a "Project brief will include this solution" note and a small WhatsApp "Ask a question" secondary link. No purchase promises. Concepts and illustrative price/time labels must remain readable.

Use ONLY provided product-specific visible text below; concise labels inside demo are allowed. Match the elegant whitespace and scanability of a very refined premium product page. Avoid repeating the same information in multiple boxes, 3-column body grids, excessive tiny icons, noisy neon glows, filler paragraphs, dense infographics or canvas-wide dashboards filled with numbers. Make it beautiful through proportion and typography.
REFERENCE: The supplied image is the NEW spacious CanveliqSoft Commerce UI Kit template. Use exactly this clean page structure, generous spacing, type scale, subtle colours, understated accordions and bottom sticky action bar. Replace the product and its content with the following. No Maison Velour perfume visuals or copied UI kit wording in this product's hero. Preserve the SINGLE small top-left progress rail; never repeat it beside every section. Never add tiny descriptive paragraphs or more cards. Do not write section numbers or duplicate little section names outside the main column. Keep the page as readable and visually quiet as this reference. Retain all ten blocks in order.
01 Breadcrumb "Collection / Retail & commerce", badge "Concept preview", title "StockFlow", purple line "Stock and orders, made clear." One sentence "See what you have, what sold, and what needs restocking."
02 ONE spacious navy inventory dashboard preview, brand StockFlow only, modest left sidebar Inventory / Orders / Reports, three large readable sample metrics "842 Products", "128 Orders", "12 Low stock", simple cyan/purple 7-bar chart with no busy labels, 3 sample inventory rows. One small mobile preview optional. Caption "Illustrative interface · Sample data". "Try sample ↗".
03 "Is this for you?" with "For small shops and growing retail teams." Three ticks "Too many spreadsheets", "Orders hard to follow", "Reorders left too late". Simple purple "Check my fit · 3 quick questions →" button.
04 "What gets easier" with just three short benefits "See stock at a glance.", "Follow each order.", "Spot what needs restocking." No paragraphs.
05 "What's included" with first accordion open "Core modules −": "Inventory & orders", "Customer records", "Low-stock alerts". Other CLOSED rows "Reports & exports +" and "Integrations & exclusions +". NO screen library, no dense icons.
06 "A day with it" simple roomy three-step mini demo "1 Receive stock → 2 Make a sale → 3 Check stock". Show a ceramic mug quantity 24 then a simple −3 sale and 21 remaining, no detailed spreadsheet. Cyan "Simulate a sale →" button. Caption "A simple sample. No live business data."
07 "How we deliver" spaced steps "Discover → Configure → Test → Handover". "Example setup: 1–3 weeks. Scope confirmed together." Closed row "See the delivery steps +".
08 "Investment" large "$29–$79 / month", immediately "Illustrative subscription range". One line "Team size, locations and integrations shape the price." Closed row "What changes the price? +".
09 "Good to know" three CLOSED rows "Licence & your data +", "Support & requirements +", "What's not included +". One readable line "Availability and support confirmed before purchase."
10 Navy band "Bring your stock into focus." Cyan "Discuss this solution →", secondary "Ask a question on WhatsApp ↗", note "Project brief will include this solution."
Ending "You may also need", two simple links Commerce UI Kit / Retail ERP with one short descriptor each. Bottom stickybar StockFlow / Save / Discuss this solution. Footer "Design preview · Example pricing, not a confirmed offer."
